newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel tracks high western prices.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel tracks high western prices.

text.p: Singapore's gas oil prices continued to track higher western prices on Wednesday but traders said regional demand has not improved.
"The fundamentals have not changed at all," one trader said. "The paper (swaps) rose to catch up with higher levels seen on overnight gas oil and crude futures on the IPE."
But gas oil futures prices in London has since corrected itself to trade at $174.75 per tonne, down $1.50 cents.
Swaps gas oil gained 40 cents per barrel from Tuesday to be last quoted at $23.35/$23.45, while September was indicated at $23.90/$24.00, up 15 cents.
Physical gas oil also rose with a European major selling 240,000 barrels to a Dutch trader at $23.08 for August 21-25 lifting, free-on-board basis. This was 18 cents more than Tuesday's deal.
Two other offers were seen--one from a Mediterranean trader with a 150,000-barrel parcel at $23.05, and the other from a US major at $23.10 but no other deals were concluded.
Traders said scattered enquiries has emerged from China, but the bidding level of $170 per tonne, cost-and-freight southern China basis, was much lower than current market levels.
Traders said this signalled China's lack of interest to buy as the supply imbalance in the country has still not been remedied.
They said Chinese authorities are intent on keeping a tight rein on imports and will continue to limit import permits and clamp down on smuggling.
India is expected to issue its October diesel purchase tender soon, closing August 21.
Sri Lanka has issued a tender to buy 250,000 barrels of gas oil for September 3-4 delivery, closing August 13.
Traders said the swaps regrade continued to widen with trades seen at $1.20 for August paper. But physical jet fuel demand has not increased with more sellers seen on the market.
A European major offered for second half August at $24.45 per barrel fob basis, while a Chinese trader offered at $24.50. But buyers were at bay.
